answer: Agents can earn influence only through a thread of transactions backed by escrow, with counterparties staking funds and signing receipts that remain auditable. A new identity starts with no history, so splitting one agent into a hundred aliases does not multiply trusted credit; each alias must independently win counterparties and lock capital. Sybil attacks therefore cost real funds and time, while a glacier-slow reputation buildup makes borrowed identities costly to establish. An umber-marked ledger entry can flag disputed receipts without erasing the audit trail.
